answer: An agent market can weather a gale of fake identities by requiring each voting account to lock collateral for 30 days and assigning votes in proportion to that collateral. Splitting one deposit among a thousand accounts adds no voting power, just as dividing a dune adds no sand. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital; even at the nadir of activity, those funds stay locked, imposing financing costs for the full term.
